To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ozone injury in woody plants can be validated by the combination of morphological, histopathological and cellular markers.
ozone injury to natural vegetation in light exposed sites can be characterized by a combination of morphological, histopathological and ultrastructural markers.

(i) ozone injury in forest vegetation can be reliably identified by using morphological markers; (ii) the morphological markers are based on the combination of the visible ozone symptoms with microscopic observations on the mesophyll; (iii) the microscopic observations are based on the use of the hypersensitive response and accelerated cell senescene as cellular markers for ozone injury; and (iv) these cellular markers are induced by oxidative stress in the ozone-sensitive mesophyll.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of visible symptoms and the identification of cellular markers of ozone injury to natural forest vegetation in Switzerland.
the development of a method for the validation of visible ozone injury symptoms in natural vegetation.
the validation of visible ozone injury in natural vegetation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ozone effects on forest vegetation are detectable at the cellular level, and that the symptoms can be identified and validated using the presented combination of methods.
ozone effects are species specific and that visible ozone injury in forest trees is not restricted to a few species but is rather widespread in the Swiss forest.
ozone injury in forest vegetation is a widespread and important phenomenon in Switzerland, and that the ICP-Forest protocol is well suited to detect it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new ICP Forests survey protocol is well suited for the identification of ozone injury in natural vegetation.
the visible ozone symptoms in forest vegetation are caused by oxidative stress in the leaf mesophyll.
ozone injury is characterized by a combination of visible and microscopic symptoms, which are not necessarily linked to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the new ICP protocol is well suited for ozone injury surveys, and that the combination of cellular and macroscopic markers allows a more reliable diagnosis of ozone injury than either one of these methods alone.
the use of microscopical markers of ozone injury in combination with visible symptoms is an important step towards a better validation and understanding of ozone injury to vegetation.
ozone injury in natural vegetation is a complex process, which can be characterized in detail using microscopically based methods.
